learningObjective: Distinguish ReduceScatter from AllReduce and identify how the two compose.

canonicalClaims.claim: ReduceScatter reduces per-rank inputs of shape S element-wise and distributes disjoint 1/N-sized shards of the result to each rank; equivalently, AllReduce is semantically equivalent to ReduceScatter followed by AllGather.
conditions: All ranks contribute inputs of the same shape S and dtype.
The reduction axis is understood; the scatter axis partitions S into N disjoint contiguous shards.
nonImplications: Does not imply that ReduceScatter is cheaper than AllReduce for the same payload — it costs (N-1)/N · S per rank, half of ring-AllReduce.
Does not imply that a subsequent AllGather is always cheaper than starting from AllReduce; you pay for both phases either way.

sourceMappings.locator: §2/§3 use of ReduceScatter for weight-sharded training

misconceptions.claim: ReduceScatter is a strict subset of AllReduce: it performs the same reduction but only returns the result to rank 0.
misconceptions.whyWrong: That description matches Reduce, not ReduceScatter. ReduceScatter returns disjoint shards of the reduced tensor to every rank.

misconceptions.claim: ReduceScatter and AllGather are inverses: applying both in either order recovers the original per-rank inputs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AllGather ∘ ReduceScatter equals AllReduce (a reduction), which is not the identity; per-rank inputs are lost.

misconceptions.claim: ReduceScatter is only useful for FSDP; it has no role in classical data-parallel gradient synchronization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Ring-AllReduce is internally implemented as ReduceScatter + AllGather; it is a standard building block, not FSDP-specific.
